# Ghaṭajātaka (Ja 355)
**ID:** Ja 355
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Ghaṭajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja355

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ghaṭajātaka* (Ja 355) is a canonical Jātaka tale preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. In the introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha, residing at Jetavana, delivers the discourse concerning a minister of the king of Kosala [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The minister had served his king faithfully, but was imprisoned on the basis of slander; while confined in prison, he attained the path of stream-entry (*sotāpattimagga*) [Fausböll 1883].
In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was born in Benares as Prince Ghaṭa (*Ghaṭakumāra*), the son of King Brahmadatta's chief queen [Fausböll 1883; Fausböll 1897]. After completing his education at Takkasilā, he ruled righteously [Fausböll 1883]. When a corrupt minister whom he had banished incited King Vaṅka of Sāvatthi against him, King Vaṅka witnessed Prince Ghaṭa seated serenely in the air and questioned why his face remained clear and bright when others would mourn [Fausböll 1883]. The opening stanza begins, *Aññe socanti rodanti* ("While others weep and wail..."), to which Prince Ghaṭa replies that sorrow neither restores the past nor ensures future happiness (*nabbhātītaharo soko nânāgatasukhāvaho*), and hence he has no reason to grieve [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. In modern scholarship, Maurice Winternitz notes the prose of the *Ghaṭa-Jātaka* (No. 355) in his discussion of the composition and layers of the Jātaka commentary [Winternitz 1933].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify thematic or verse resemblances with several canonical and para-canonical texts, including verse 98 of the Dhammapada (Dhp 98), the *Khāntivagga* of the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 239–260), the *Rāmaṇeyyakasutta* (SN 11.15), the *Sāriputtattheragāthā* (Thag 17.2), Chinese Dharmapada recensions (T 210.15 and T 212.30), and the *Yugavarga* of the Udānavarga traditions (UV 29, Uv Kg 29) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates internal Pali text reuse with the commentary, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), sharing seven text segments (including §2.2–5.4 matching §1424–1433) [DharmaNexus].

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): dhp98; P-Dhp 239–260 Khāntivagga; SN 11.15 Rāmaṇeyyakasutta; T 210.15 羅漢品法句經第十五有十章; T 212.30 雙要品第三十; Thag 17.2 Sāriputtattheragāthā; UV 29 Yugavarga; Uv Kg 29 Day and Night
